## Armistice acknowledgments, personnel and Warsaw radio inquiries

**Sources on this page:** p203 A2, p203 B.

**Related source pages:** [p202 A1](202.md#source-p202-a1), [p202 A2](202.md#source-p202-a2), [p204 B](204.md#source-p204-b), [p204 C1](204.md#source-p204-c1), [p204 D](204.md#source-p204-d).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-armistice-acknowledgments-personnel-and-warsaw-radio-inquiries"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Seven native source records cover an armistice-receipt query, nightly radio listening, an inquiry for Captain von Borries, the location of the Warsaw general government, and radio equipment and personnel. Two previously OCR-damaged short messages become clear when their actually printed final groups are restored. All unresolved fields and missing-letter spellings remain explicit.

<a id="source-p203-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-p203-a2"></a>

### p203 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) --- v ZON (23.31 p.m., November 16th); 22.35 (16/11); 2 TL RIZI-132`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> Stehet jede Nacht auf Empfang. Verbindung mit Deutschl. dringend benoetigt.

**Meaning:** Maintain reception every night; a connection with Germany is urgently needed. Only the source-labelled second part is present in this record.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
STE?ETJEDEN?CHTAUF?MPFANGXVERBINDUNGMITDEUTSCHLXRRINGENDBENOETIGTX
```

**Edited output** — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 2 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
STEHETJEDENACHTAUFEMPFANGXVERBINDUNGMITDEUTSCHLXDRINGENDBENOETIGTX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The printed 2 TL is retained. The absent first part is not reconstructed from this second part.
- Two opening dashes are source-mask slots. The unchanged Nov13–15b key produces this body despite the printed 16 November date; this is a documented key-use observation, not a silent redating.
- DEUTSCHL remains the transmitted abbreviation.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-p203-b"></a>

### p203 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) IWE v LP (03.48 p.m., November 18th); FUER IWE v LP 14.55 (18/11); RICHI-164`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> KM Abt. Nachrichtenmittel erbittet Nachricht ueber Verbleib Hptm. v. Borries, Gen. Kdo. ?2.

**Meaning:** The War Ministry communications-equipment section asks for information on the whereabouts of Captain von Borries. The general-command label ?2 is not numbered historically.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
KMXABTXNACHRICHTENMITTELXERBITTETNACHRICHTUEBERVERBLEIBXHPTMXVXBORRIESXGENXKDOX?2X
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The OCR omitted the final four-coordinate group GVFD. The source visibly prints it, and restoring it yields the exact advertised 164-slot frame. This is a transcription correction, not a historical coordinate insertion.
- The body names VXBORRIES; no specific person is identified from the surname alone.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are preserved separately. This is a source edition and explicit repair review, not a claim of universal first-decipherment priority.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For partial outputs, each certificate also constructs one injective global completion of the square and residual masks and verifies its full round-trip; the witness is explicitly nonhistorical. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

### p202 A1

**Source transcription — header:** `A) NKJ, UKS v LP (12.51 p.m., November 16th); FUER UKS 0900 (16), 2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-212`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> An OKM. Sofortige Bestaetigung erforderlich, ob Funkspruch 1XAXC?XR vom 1RX11 betr. Waffenstillstandsbedingungen

**Meaning:** Immediate confirmation is requested that a telegram on armistice conditions has arrived. The reference and date labels remain unresolved; the sentence continues in A2.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ANXOKMXXSOFORTIGEBESTAETIGUNGERFORDERLICHOBFUNKSYRUCHX1XAXC?XRXVOM1RX11MBETRXNAFFDNSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGENX
```

**Edited output** — 4 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text

```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The word repairs include FUNKSYRUCH to FUNKSPRUCH, M to separator X before BETR, and NAFFDN to WAFFEN. All resulting coordinate changes are priced. The opaque C?XR and 1RX11 fields are not guessed.

**Source transcription — header:** `A) same two-part telegram; 2 TL RICHI-142`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> und Befehl zur Fortsetzung des Abmarsches dort angekommen. OHL 1XAXNRX1???12XOP.

### p204 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v WAU (1.50 a.m., November 18th); 0115 (17), 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-244`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> GE?NACH2O2. Leichte in Lomza und Czenstochau, Verbleib unbekannt. Vermutl. mit ihren Gouvs. aberueckt. Besatzg beiden anderen Stat. ohne Geraet.

**Meaning:** The whereabouts of the light units or equipment in Lomza and Czenstochau are unknown; they are presumed to have departed with their governors. The crews of the other two stations have no equipment. The opening is opaque and several transmitted abbreviations and the missing-letter spelling ABERUECKT remain visible.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
GE?NACH2O2LE?CHTEINLOMZAUNDCZENSTOCHAUXV?RBLEIBUNBEKANNTXVERMUTLMITI?RENGOUVSABERUECKTXBESATZGBEIDENANDERE?STATOHNEGERA?TX
```

**Edited output** — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 3 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
GE?NACH2O2LEICHTEINLOMZAUNDCZENSTOCHAUXVERBLEIBUNBEKANNTXVERMUTLMITIHRENGOUVSABERUECKTXBESATZGBEIDENANDERENSTATOHNEGERAETX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The source prints four dash slots: XD--- and GG-AX. The opening GE?NACH2O2 remains unresolved.
- The source-length output ABERUECKT is not silently expanded to [abgerueckt]. VERMUTL, GOUVS, BESATZG and STAT remain their transmitted abbreviated forms.
- Part 2 advertises 282 slots but the reviewed page prints 242. A 40-slot tail-loss hypothesis yields related fragments, but is not accepted as a complete source-length decipherment or counted as another reviewed reading here.

### p204 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) --- v --- (8.43 a.m., November 18th); RICHI-84`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> Zu 2??F vom 1?X: 1. Nein. 2. PSO BSL. Fusta WAU.

**Meaning:** A short numbered reply answers no to item 1 and gives the literal call-sign-like pair PSO BSL for item 2. The inquiry number, date and expansion of PSO remain unresolved.

With the [existing shared-order assignment VA=5](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md),
the date-like field becomes **15X**. The record then fixes **40/42** positions;
the inquiry number stays `2??F`. This is a consequence of the p201/p206
order-date comparison, with no additional source edit.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ZU2??FVOM1?XX1XNEINXX2XPSOXBSLXXFUSTAWAUXX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The source visibly prints VAXAX and the final AXGF, both omitted from the earlier OCR candidate. The native count is 84.
- The baseline quotation keeps `1?X` before the sentence separator; the shared-order layer gives `15X`.

</details>

## p203 C — Inquiry about Richter at the Aleppo radio park

**Edition context:** p203 C / p210 C — inquiries about Richter in Aleppo.

**Related source pages:** [p210 C](210.md#source-p210-c).

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-p203-c--p210-c--inquiries-about-richter-in-aleppo"></a>


[Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json)

**Records:** two related personnel inquiries, on 18 and 20 November 1918,
under different published period keys. **Result:** the earlier message
fixes **93 of 96 raw positions** without any source edit. The later fixes
**201 of 204**, and its readable body requires six coordinate substitutions
and three source-erasure fills. Their postal-number fields differ; they
are not forced into one recovered number.

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-the-earlier-inquiry-p203-c"></a>

### The earlier inquiry, p203 C

**Readable German:**

> K.M., Abt. Nachrichtenmittel, erbittet Nachricht Verbleib Untffz.
> Richter, Funkerpark Aleppo, Feldpost ???.

**Meaning:** The War Ministry's communications-equipment section asks
for news of the whereabouts of an NCO named Richter at the radio park
in Aleppo. Its field-post number remains unresolved.

The source abbreviation **UNTFFZ** is retained. Its interpretation as an
NCO is supported by the later message's directly read **UNTEROFFZ**.
The earlier message itself does not supply the first name Kurt.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KMXABTXNACHRICHTENMITTELXERBITTETNACHRICHTVERBLEIBUNTFFZXRICHTERXFUNKERPARKXALEPPOXFELDPOSTX???X
```

</details>

All **192** coordinates in [p203 C](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p203_C.png)
are valid and unchanged. The three question marks are unknown square-cell
values, not damaged source glyphs. The source section belongs to the
**18 November** heading, below an earlier 16 November section:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
XYZ v LP (03.51 p.m., November 18th)
IWE KOW AS FUER XYZ 14.50 (18/11)
RICHI-192
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-the-later-inquiry-p210-c"></a>

### The later inquiry, p210 C

The same-length editorial reconstruction reads:

**Readable German:**

> Ist ueber den Unteroffz. Kurt Richter, Aleppo, Armeenachrichtenpark
> J527, Deutsche Feldpost 227, Auskunft ueber jetzigen Standort oder
> Verbleib zu erfahren? [Raw following character: J.]
> Nr. Q90 strich JJ, J4, A. Nch. Kriegsminist., Allgem.
> Kriegsdepartement.

**Meaning:** The later message asks whether information can be obtained
about the current location or whereabouts of NCO Kurt Richter in Aleppo,
giving an Army Signals Park designation and field-post number. The name
**KURT RICHTER**, Aleppo, and **FELDPOST227** are directly read.
The designation **J527**, references **Q90 / JJ / J4**, and the isolated
`J` following `ERFAHREN` remain literal. They are not silently converted to
numerals or a reconstructed reference.

The [p210 C source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p210_C.png)
has **408** coordinate slots and this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
XYZ v LP (02.55 p.m., November 20th)
17.40 (20/11)
RICHI-408
```

</details>

Its raw decipherment under the unchanged Nov19–21 key is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
IS0XEBERDENUNTEROFFZXKURTXRICHTERXALEPPOXARMEENACHRICHTENPARKXJ527XDEUTSCLEFELDPOSTX227XAUSKUNFTUEBER3ETZIGENSTANDORTOWERVERBLEIBZUERFAHRENJXNRXQ90STRICHJJXJ4XAXNCHX?RIEGSMINISTXALLGEMXK?I?GSDEPARTEMENTXX
```

</details>

The invalid source glyphs in **AFEVF**, **CXVVA** and **EGFDF** retain
their positions in the literal transcript. For analysis, they are masked
as erasures at source indices **302, 365 and 385**. The candidate fills
those slots with **F, G and F**, respectively. The remaining body repairs
change six valid coordinates:

| Source index, zero-based | Source | Proposed |
| ---: | :---: | :---: |
| 50 | G | X |
| 61 | G | F |
| 230 | A | X |
| 265 | A | X |
| 316 | G | F |
| 378 | X | V |

These give the readable opening `IST UEBER`, `DEUTSCHE`, `JETZIGEN`,
`ODER` and the War Ministry closing. The candidate preserves **399 valid
source coordinates** and re-encrypts exactly after the six changes and
three fills. It adds no plaintext letters and does not change the key.
The question mark in the spaced German is editorial punctuation; the
following literal `J` is explicitly acknowledged above.

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-why-the-postal-number-is-not-transferred-across-keys"></a>

### Constraints on the cross-key postal-number comparison

The shared surname, rank and Aleppo location support reading these as
related inquiries. They do not establish that the address fields were
identical or copied without error.

| Message and positions | Printed-key result | Observed pairs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| p203 C, 92–94 | `???` | `VA VA VV` under Nov16–18 |
| p210 C, 84–86 | `227` | `DG DG DA` under Nov19–21 |

The earlier first two digits are one shared unknown, and the last digit
must be different under an injective square. The base domain for each
cell is `{0,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}`. The later **227** cannot simply be copied back:
that would put `2` at **VA**, while the unchanged Nov16–18 square already
puts `2` at **DV**. The coordinate certificate checks this conflict.

The separate [p201/p206 order-date inference](201.md#edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders)
conditionally assigns **VA=5**. If accepted, it would make this earlier
field `55?`; it would not settle the mismatch with `227`. This edition
preserves the evidence without selecting a changed address, a copying
error, or a different digit labelling as the explanation.

### Source, reproduction and credit

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp203 and 210 / PDF page 206 and 213 in the
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source package](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/README.md) preserves
literal rows, source images, complete published key snapshots and every
plaintext-to-coordinate map. The existing keys retain their external
attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, related-message comparison and this edition:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_recovery/verify.py --verify
```
